_about: Photogrammetry-style (AI) models of San Francisco landmarks: their source files and what tools/modelpack/pack.ts needs to make game-ready LODs of them. Intrinsic facts only (real size, which axis is the front, waterline, material); where a project puts one is that project's business (cityengine: public/landmarks/san-francisco-statues.json).

_fields.id: asset id in the assetkit-models-sf index
_fields.material: 'textured' (the file carries its own texture), else a shader for an untextured model: bronze (the default), copperoxide, concrete, whitestone, silver… (a material named in the file name wins)
_fields.front: the model's own axis its front faces, as the glTF loader leaves it: +z | -z | +x | -x
_fields.scale: { axis: x|y|z, metres }: the real size along that model axis; the whole model is scaled uniformly from it (a ship by its length, a statue by its height)
_fields.draft: ships: metres from the model's lowest point up to the waterline, after scaling
_fields.plinth: statues whose model has no base: the pedestal a renderer must draw, [width, depth, height] metres; absent when the model brings its own or stands on the ground
_fields.lods: levels to make: ratio of triangles kept (1 = all), texture cap in px, and the simplifier's error limit (fraction of the model's size; default 0.02 — a far LOD of a rigged ship needs more, or the thin lines stop it)
_fields.crop: optional { axis, max }: triangles whose middle is further than max (model units) from the centre along axis are dropped — a stray rope sticking out
_fields.squash: optional { axis, factor }: scale one axis only, for a model the AI stretched (the Pampanito came out twice as tall as she is)

models.name: Balclutha (1886 full-rigged ship)
models.description: Steel-hulled three-masted full-rigged ship built 1886 by Charles Connell & Co., Glasgow; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: Model length (z, 1.0 unit) runs from the bowsprit tip to the stern: 92 m overall (301 ft). The red bottom (antifouling) is about 8% of the length, and she floats light: in the 2012 photo (3-context.jpg) the upper part of the red shows, so the waterline is 4.5 m above the model's lowest point (2026-10-18). Her bow points toward the pier's shore end, by the Eureka (the same photo; about.md's 'north-west' is wrong). Two LODs only: the simplifier stops at ~8 k triangles whatever the error limit (the rigging is hundreds of separate textured strips with UV seams), and most of the memory is the texture; beyond lod1's range a game draws its own stand-in (cityengine: the procedural ship).

models.name: C.A. Thayer (1895 lumber schooner)
models.description: Three-masted wooden lumber schooner built 1895 by Hans Bendixsen, Fairhaven CA; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: Model x runs over 67 m overall (219 ft, bowsprit and boom). A stray rope stood ~0.24 units out to the side (owner, 2026-10-18: 'may interfere with nearby objects'): cropped at |z| > 0.13 (the hull's half-beam is 0.084, deck fittings reach 0.12). Draft ~3.5 m (depth of hold).

models.name: Alma (1891 scow schooner)
models.description: Flat-bottomed San Francisco Bay scow schooner built 1891 at Hunters Point; museum ship of the San Francisco Maritime NHP.
models.notes: 18 m on deck; the model's z runs from the bowsprit tip past the boom, ~25 m. Its lowest point is the lowered leeboard, ~2.4 m below the hull, so the waterline (1.1 m draft) is ~3.5 m above it. Sails set, as Tripo made her.

models.name: Hercules (1907 steam tug)
models.description: Ocean-going steam tug built 1907 by John H. Dialogue & Son, Camden NJ; museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: 46 m (151 ft); draft 5.5 m aft, ~4.5 m mean.

models.name: SS Jeremiah O'Brien (1943 Liberty ship)
models.description: Liberty ship built 1943 at the New England Shipbuilding Corporation, South Portland, Maine; one of two operational Liberty ships, museum ship in San Francisco.
models.notes: 134.6 m (441 ft 6 in); laden draft 8.5 m, as a museum ship riding higher, ~6 m.

models.name: USS Pampanito (1943 submarine)
models.description: Balao-class fleet submarine launched 1943 at Portsmouth Navy Yard; museum ship at Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf.
models.notes: 95 m (311 ft 6 in); surfaced draft ~4.6 m; the red bottom is below the waterline. Tripo made her 0.43 units tall to 1.0 long: 41 m at 95 m, against ~17-19 m keel to the top of the periscope shears; squashed in y by 0.47.

models.name: Taj Mahal houseboat, Sausalito
models.description: A houseboat in the form of a miniature Taj Mahal, Sausalito.
models.notes: An easter egg (owner, 2026-10-18). Size estimated (~14 m long on its float); its arched entrance is on -x.

models.name: Eureka (1890 paddle-wheel ferry)
models.description: Side-wheel walking-beam passenger and car ferry built 1890 (as Ukiah, rebuilt 1922 as Eureka); museum ship at Hyde Street Pier.
models.notes: 91 m overall (299 ft 6 in), 24 m over the guards; double-ended, so either end is its front. Model 'based on mini' (owner, 2026-10-18).

models.name: Victory, Dewey Monument
models.description: Bronze Victory with trident and wreath on a globe atop the Dewey Monument's column, Union Square (1903).
models.notes: Untextured: shade as copperoxide (named in the file). Scaled from the owner's photograph (2026-10-18): figure with globe ~2.45 x the shaft's diameter under the capital, which Wikipedia gives as 5 ft (1.5 m): ~3.8 m — a 9 ft figure (Wikipedia) plus the globe; the marker's 'twelve foot' would be the figure with her raised trident. On the 85 ft column (cityengine draws it). SUPERSEDED 2026-10-18 by dewey-monument (capital included); kept for reference.

models.name: Mechanics Monument
models.description: Bronze group of five mechanics working a punch press, Market and Battery Streets (1901), honouring Peter Donahue.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model carries the lower granite base; ~7.5 m overall.

models.name: Mahatma Gandhi, Ferry Building
models.description: Bronze striding Gandhi with his staff, at the Ferry Building (1988).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. 8 ft (2.4 m) striding figure on its rough bronze base (Wikipedia, 'Statue of Mahatma Gandhi (San Francisco)'), on a block with a plaque raised on two steps — a long low block, wider than deep, in the Commons photo (drawn by the renderer).

models.name: Willie Mays, Oracle Park
models.description: Bronze Willie Mays at the swing, Willie Mays Plaza, Oracle Park (2000).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model has its own thin base; on a granite pedestal ~1.5 m (drawn by the renderer).

models.name: Abraham Lincoln, City Hall
models.description: Seated bronze Lincoln on the Polk Street side of City Hall (1928).
models.notes: Untextured: BRONZE (owner's photo, 2026-10-18: 'I was wrong it is actually bronze' — the file name says copperoxide). Seated figure with chair and its base ~2.9 m, on a pale granite die about as tall as the seated figure, a little wider than deep, on a base course (drawn by the renderer). The die just fits the statue's own base (owner): 1.95 x 2.15 m, 2.0 m tall.

models.name: Dewey Monument top (capital and Victory)
models.artist: Robert Ingersoll Aitken (figure), Newton J. Tharp (column)
models.description: The top of the Dewey Monument, Union Square (1903): the Corinthian capital, the drum and globe, and the bronze Victory with trident and wreath.
models.notes: Textured (white stone capital, verdigris figure). Its foot is the capital's neck, 0.208 model units across = the shaft's 5 ft (1.5 m, Wikipedia) under the capital: 7.2 m tall. Sits on a plain cylinder (cityengine draws the shaft). Supersedes dewey-victory (figure only).

models.name: Dewey Monument top (capital and Victory), PBR
models.artist: Robert Ingersoll Aitken (figure), Newton J. Tharp (column)
models.description: The top of the Dewey Monument, Union Square (1903): the Corinthian capital, the drum and globe, and the bronze Victory with trident and wreath.
models.notes: The same mesh as dewey-monument with Tripo's PBR textures (base colour + metallic-roughness). Packed to compare with the plain textured one (owner, 2026-10-18).

models.name: Admission Day Monument, the flag-waving miner
models.description: Bronze young Native Son with a flag over his shoulder, at the foot of the Admission Day Monument column (1897).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the miner and his flag only (no base, no column). 3.2 m is a guess: a ~2.2 m figure plus the raised flag. Front -z: the stride and the head point toward -z in the +x view. The column and Genius figure are not in the model; the granite step it stands on is a 0.9 m plinth.

models.name: The Cider Press, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Bronze group of a youth hauling on a cider press lever, a boy crouched at its foot (1892).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. 2.5 m (about.md). The model brings its own stone base. Front +z: the +z view shows the youth's chest and hands on the lever; -z shows his back. 15 000/4 000-triangle budget as a group.

models.name: Ruth Asawa's Andrea fountain figures, Ghirardelli Square
models.description: Two bronze mermaids with turtles, frogs and lily pads, from the Andrea fountain (1968).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the figures only, no basin, 1.0 x 1.0 units wide. OSM's pool (way 939539789) is 5.2 m across, so 1 unit = 5 m and the height is 0.39 x 5 = 1.9 m (a seated mermaid then ~1.45 m, about.md says ~1.2). No obvious front; +z chosen.

models.name: Ashurbanipal, Civic Center
models.description: Bronze Assyrian king Ashurbanipal carrying a lion cub and a tablet, by the Main Library (1988).
models.notes: Textured (dark bronze, 5 MB jpeg: shrunk to 512/256). Wikipedia: 15 ft (4.6 m) overall; Parhad's site says 8 ft for the figure, so 2.5 m figure on a 2.0 m pedestal. Front -x: the face and tablet show in the -x view. LOD1 would not simplify below ~7.9k triangles at error 0.02 (UV seams), so its error limit is 0.1.

models.name: Beethoven bust, Music Concourse
models.description: Bronze bust of Beethoven on a granite pedestal, Golden Gate Park (1915).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model is the bust with a small socle (~1.3 m, about.md says ~1 m bust); the tall granite shaft with the muse is a 2.2 m plinth. Front -x (the face in the -x view).

models.name: Benjamin Franklin, Washington Square
models.description: Bronze Franklin in 18th-century dress holding a paper, on a tall granite drinking-fountain pedestal (1879).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The file is named city_hall but the about.md (Washington Square) is the one used; a standing coat-and-breeches Franklin with a paper in hand matches both. 2.4 m figure on a ~3.4 m granite pedestal. Front -x.

models.name: Bufano's St. Francis, Fisherman's Wharf
models.description: Monolithic hooded granite St. Francis with arms spread, at Taylor and Beach (Frank Cresci Plaza).
models.notes: Untextured: the granite is drawn as concrete. 18 ft (5.5 m), 12-20 tons of granite (Kerouac.com, HMDB). The model has its own tapered base. Front -x (the hooded face shows in the -x view).

models.name: Bufano's Peace, Brotherhood Way
models.description: Bufano's 38 ft Peace (1958): a hooded stainless-steel figure with gold leaf, granite and tile mosaic, a gift of the San Francisco Chronicle; first at the airport, since 1996 beside the dog park on Brotherhood Way.
models.notes: Textured. About 38 ft (11.6 m) overall (SF Arts Commission / ARG Conservation). The model has its own round base. Front -x (the face and rose robe show in the -x view). Peace stands at 800 Brotherhood Way, inside San Francisco (SFO was its first home).

models.name: Bufano's Penguins, Gateway Commons
models.description: Bufano's simplified granite penguin with a small chick at its feet and a red-capped beak, on an octagonal base.
models.notes: Textured (grey granite, red beak). About 1.8 m including its octagonal base (about.md says 1.5-2 m; the base is part of the model). Front +z (the chick and crossed feet show in the +z view).

models.name: Cervantes Monument, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Jo Mora's Cervantes Monument (1916): a bronze bust on a granite boulder, Don Quixote and Sancho Panza kneeling at its foot.
models.notes: Textured. About 3.5 m overall (about.md: 3-3.5 m, bust and boulder). The boulder is its own base. Front -z: the bust's collar, the scroll and the kneeling figures face -z.

models.name: General Pershing, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Haig Patigian's bronze General Pershing (1922), a German helmet at his feet, on a tall granite pedestal at the Music Concourse.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The figure is about 2.6 m with its thin base; the granite pedestal (~3.2 m) is drawn by the renderer. Front -z (the face and the helmet's side show in the -z view).

models.name: Chinatown guardian lion, Dragon Gate
models.description: Seated Chinese guardian lion (shishi) in carved granite, one of the pair at the Dragon Gate, Grant Avenue at Bush.
models.notes: Untextured: granite drawn as concrete. One model, placed twice (a pair, mirrored in bearing). Front -x (the face shows in the -x view). 1.4 m including its own base, on a ~0.6 m pedestal.

models.name: Goddess of Democracy, Portsmouth Square
models.artist: Thomas Marsh and Shanghai/Beijing Central Academy of Fine Arts students (replica of the 1989 Tiananmen statue)
models.description: Bronze woman holding a torch aloft in both hands, a 1994 replica of the Tiananmen Square 'Goddess of Democracy', in Portsmouth Square, Chinatown.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. About 3 m including the model's own thin slab; the real figure stands on a pale granite block about 0.9 m high (Commons photo), drawn by the renderer. Front -x (torch at the left, hair swept right in the -x view, as in the Commons 3/4 photo).

models.name: Joseph Strauss, Golden Gate Bridge
models.description: Bronze Joseph B. Strauss, chief engineer of the Golden Gate Bridge, in a three-piece suit with rolled plans, on the Strauss Legacy Circle at the bridge's south end.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. ~2.5 m figure including the model's own small bronze slab; it stands on a low round grey disc (Legacy Circle, ~0.4 m) which is not drawn. Front -x (tie and plans show in the -x view).

models.name: The Lone Sailor, Vista Point
models.description: Bronze US Navy sailor in a peacoat with a sea bag on a bollard, on a red granite plinth: the Lone Sailor replica at Vista Point beside the Golden Gate Bridge.
models.notes: Textured; the model carries its own red polished granite base (the figure ~2.1 m on a ~0.4 m base: 2.5 m overall). Front -x (face and sea bag toward the camera in the -x view, as in the Commons photos).

models.name: Lotta's Fountain
models.description: The cast-iron fountain column at Market, Geary and Kearny Streets, given to the city by the actress Lotta Crabtree in 1875.
models.notes: Textured, bronze-coloured. About 24 ft (7.3 m) overall, the whole fountain column including its base (Wikipedia gives no height; the earlier procedural stand-in used 8 m with a 0.5 m offset). Four-sided, so the front is arbitrary (+z).

models.name: Miguel Hidalgo, Dolores Park
models.description: Bronze standing Father Miguel Hidalgo in a long coat and boots, one arm out, at the upper corner of Dolores Park (1962).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. ~3 m figure on a small rock base (the model has it); stands on a tall black granite die (~2.6 m) on a low black platform (drawn by the renderer from the Commons photo). Face seen from -x.

models.name: Pioneer Mother, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Bronze mother with two children, arm outstretched, on the stepped top of Grafly's 1915 monument (moved to Golden Gate Park in 1940).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model has the small stepped bronze top (~3 m figure, 3.3 m with it); the tall red-brown stone base with the ship relief (about 3.3 m of the ~7.9 m total) is the plinth. Face seen from -x.

models.name: Puddle Jumpers, Transamerica Redwood Park
models.description: Five bronze children running and leaping in a chain through a puddle, Transamerica Redwood Park.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. Chain of five, ~3.2 m long (children ~1.1 m, the leader leaping); no base. Leader (arm flung out) is at -z, so the group runs toward -z.

models.name: Seal balancing a ball, Seals Plaza
models.description: Bronze seal balancing a ball on its nose, on a ring base, in Seals Plaza at Oracle Park's Marina Gate.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The file is named Lou Seal (the Giants mascot); the model is a seal balancing a ball on a split-ring base, which matches the Seals Plaza sculpture outside the ballpark, so it is placed there. Height ~2 m is a guess (no source gives it). Head toward -z.

models.name: Crab topiary, Pier 39
models.description: Dark crab with raised claws, its shell planted with flowers: the crab topiary at Pier 39.
models.notes: Textured. Height ~2.5 m is a guess (no source found); front taken as -x (claws up toward the viewer).

models.name: Guardians of the Gate sea lions, Pier 39
models.description: Everdur bronze family of sea lions on a rock base, West Park beside Pier 39 (1992).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. The model carries its own rock base. Real size 4 ft 6 in x 8 ft x 5 ft (public-art list; which is height is not stated), so 1.4 m high. Front +x (guess: the two animals face that way).

models.name: Spanish bronze cannon, Presidio
models.description: Spanish bronze cannon on a concrete block, as on the Presidio's Main Post (Pershing Square and the Officers' Club).
models.notes: Textured. Barrel ~2.3 m (guess: NPS gives no length); the model has its concrete mounting block. Muzzle toward +z (bore seen from +z).

models.name: Robert Louis Stevenson Memorial galleon, Portsmouth Square
models.description: The bronze galleon with sails set on its carved wave base, the finial of the Robert Louis Stevenson Memorial in Portsmouth Square.
models.notes: Textured. The model is only the ship and its carved base (the granite shaft, ~10 ft, is drawn by the procedural stevensonMemorial), so it is attached on top of that shaft. Ship long axis is z with the bowsprit at +z (front). 1.1 m overall height is a guess (no source gives it): the procedural stand-in's galleon is ~1 m long. A monument finial, not a boat: it floats on nothing.

models.name: Roman Gladiator, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Bronze gladiator with a raised short sword and flowing cloak, on a granite pedestal with a bronze plaque, beside the de Young Museum (the 1894 Midwinter Fair commemoration).
models.notes: Textured; the model carries its own pedestal (about 40% of the height). about.md: ~2.5 m bronze figure on a stone pedestal; with the pedestal as drawn (photo 1-front.jpg: figure about 60% of the whole) that is ~4.2 m overall. Front +z: the sword-arm and outstretched arm point to +z and the cloak streams to -z; the plaque is on the +z face.

models.name: Sutro Heights gate lion
models.artist: unattributed (1880s Sutro estate; the present pair are replicas)
models.description: Recumbent stone lion with a full mane and paws stretched forward, on a rough stone slab: one of the pair flanking the entrance to Sutro Heights Park.
models.notes: The file is named sf_chinatown_stone_lion but it is a Western recumbent lion (mane, crossed paws, tail along the flank) matching the Sutro Heights reference photos, not a Chinese shishi: placed at Sutro Heights, not Chinatown. Textured (grey stone, 69 MB, 1.9 M triangles: simplified hard, 512/256 textures). ~1.5 m high incl. the model's own slab (about.md). Front guessed +x (head toward +x/+z in the previews); fixed by bearing in the placement. The ordinary simplifier stops at ~182 000 triangles here (UV seams lock the mesh), so both LODs use `sloppy` (meshopt simplifySloppy).

models.name: Perry's bronze lion, de Young
models.description: Seated bronze lion on a rock, by the de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park.
models.notes: Textured (dark green bronze). Seated lion on its own rock base; height 1.4 m is a guess (no source gives it). Front +x: the head and open mouth face +x in the +z and -z views. LOD1 over budget: the simplifier stops at ~8 200 triangles (375 kB) whatever the ratio or error (UV seams).

models.name: Buckyball, Exploratorium Pier 15
models.description: Leo Villareal's Buckyball: two nested geodesic spheres of LED nodes on a tripod standing in a railed ring, Pier 15 plaza.
models.notes: Textured. 25 ft (7.6 m) overall (Exploratorium, SF Travel). Rotationally symmetric, so the front is arbitrary (+z). 15 000/4 000-triangle budget as a monument; thin struts, so LOD1 error 0.04. LOD1 stops at ~6 500 triangles (237 kB), above the 4 000 target.

models.name: Francis Scott Key Monument, Golden Gate Park
models.description: The 1888 Francis Scott Key Monument: a travertine baldachin with the seated bronze Key under the canopy and Columbia with her flag staff above, at the east end of the Music Concourse.
models.notes: Textured scan; includes its own stepped base and the canopy, so no plinth. About 14-15 m overall (about.md estimate). Front is +z (the inscription tablet side, preview). Key himself was toppled in 2020; the model shows the intact monument.

models.name: Portrait of Georgia O'Keeffe (Marisol)
models.description: Marisol's 1982 bronze Portrait of Georgia O'Keeffe: a blocky bust-on-pedestal figure with her two chow dogs, in Sydney G. Walton Square.
models.notes: Textured scan. Height not found in sources: 1.8 m is a guess for the figure on its low pedestal (the model's irregular base slab is part of the scan). Front -x: the face and both dogs face the viewer from -x (preview).

models.name: Spire (Andy Goldsworthy), Presidio
models.description: 2008 land-art spire of 37 Monterey cypress trunks lashed in a tapering bundle, about 30 m tall, in the Presidio.
models.notes: Textured (charred dark on one side, pale on the other). The file is named golden_gate_park_spire but is the Presidio Spire. OSM height 30.48 m; rotationally near-symmetric, front arbitrary. No plinth: rises from the ground.

models.name: Hills Bros. coffee drinker
models.description: The robed Arab coffee drinker of the Hills Bros. trademark, raising his cup, as a figure on the roof of the Hills Bros. coffee works on the Embarcadero.
models.notes: Textured scan. Height is a guess (3.5 m for a rooftop figure). Front -x: he faces the viewer from -x, cup to his mouth (preview). Own small base; no plinth.

models.name: Hope / Peace hands (Giuseppe Palumbo), Pier 28
models.description: Two sculpted hands, one crossing fingers for hope and one in a V for peace, each on its own dark block; Big Art Loop, Pier 28, the Embarcadero.
models.notes: Textured scan with its two small bases. Size not published: 2.2 m is a guess. Front -x: the hands face the viewer from -x (preview); they stand side by side along z.

models.name: Padre Junipero Serra, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Douglas Tilden's 1907 bronze of Fra Junipero Serra, arm raised, holding a tall cross, on a granite pedestal on the Music Concourse.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze (green-black patina in life). Figure ~3.5-4 m on a granite pedestal ~1.5 x 1.5 x 4 m (about.md estimates; Wikipedia 9 m overall). Front -x (face, raised hand and cross seen from -x). Toppled in 2020; the model shows it standing.

models.name: La Chiffonniere (Dubuffet), Embarcadero Plaza
models.description: Dubuffet's 1978 painted-epoxy-and-stainless La Chiffonniere (the ragpicker), 6.7 m tall, in Embarcadero Plaza.
models.notes: Textured scan with its round base disc. 22 ft (6.7 m) per Public Art Fund / Wikipedia. Front -x (the face and torso panels read from -x in the preview); Dubuffet's piece has no true front.

models.name: William McKinley Memorial, the Panhandle
models.description: Victory with sword and palm on a granite pedestal, on round steps (1904), the Panhandle.
models.notes: Textured. The model brings its round steps and pedestal; ~9 m overall (OSM statue 3.05 m; the procedural stand-in is ~11 m). Front -x (the in-place render showed her back at +x).

models.name: Naga, the sea serpent
models.artist: Cjay Roughgarden, Stephanie Shipman, Jacquelyn Scott
models.description: Lighted aqua and silver sea serpent sculpture, 100 ft long (2025).
models.notes: Textured. Scaled by its 100 ft (OSM description) length along z; head taken at +z.

models.name: Node, Roxy Paine
models.description: 102 ft stainless-steel branching tower at the Yerba Buena/Moscone Muni station (2023).
models.notes: Untextured; stainless steel drawn in plaster (the greyest shader the packer knows). 102 ft (SF Chronicle). No front. Squashed to 0.4 across its lean (x): the AI model leans 0.74 of its height sideways, which tipped its top out over 4th Street; the real branch rises nearly straight from the plaza with kinks (owner, 2026-10-25).

models.name: The Ordonez Gun, Presidio
models.description: Battle-damaged Spanish gun from Subic Bay on its carriage, Pershing Square, Presidio.
models.notes: Textured. Overall length (muzzle to carriage wheel) ~3.2 m is an estimate; muzzle at -z.

models.name: Van Ness Lighting Sculpture, Jorge Pardo
models.description: Thirteen poles topped by coloured spheres, tallest ~20 ft; two sets on Van Ness Avenue.
models.notes: Textured. Tallest pole 20 ft = 6.1 m (SF Arts Commission); a row ~8.4 m long along z.

models.name: Philo T. Farnsworth, Presidio
models.description: Bronze Farnsworth, inventor of television, Letterman Digital Arts Center.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. Life-size figure with its own low base, ~2.1 m. Front -x.

models.name: Corpus, Pier 14
models.description: Corpus: a 16 ft steel creature on spindly rooted legs, Big Art Loop, Pier 14 on the Embarcadero (2025, from Burning Man).
models.notes: Untextured: bronze (the real piece is steel, the packer has no steel shader). 16 ft (4.9 m) per the Big Art Loop. Front (the end with the eye bumps) taken as +z by judgement; a temporary Big Art Loop loan (installed Oct 2025). No reference folder.

models.name: Skygate, the Embarcadero
models.description: Skygate (1985): a 26 ft silver steel gateway of twisting ribbons on the Embarcadero, dedicated to Eric Hoffer.
models.notes: Untextured; the packer has no steel shader, so plaster (pale grey) stands in for the silver. 26 ft = 7.9 m (OSM description). Symmetric, so front +z. No reference folder.

models.name: Sphinx, de Young Museum
models.description: One of a pair of reclining concrete sphinxes (c. 1910) flanking the approach to the de Young Museum, Golden Gate Park.
models.notes: Untextured: off-white concrete = plaster. The head faces -x. About 2 m tall including base: 1.6 m sphinx on a low 0.4 m plinth (the model has no base). Place twice (the museum's pair is mirrored).

models.name: Sun Yat-sen, St Mary's Square
models.description: Bufano's stainless-steel Sun Yat-sen (1937) on its pink granite base, St Mary's Square.
models.notes: Textured, with its own pink granite base, so no plinth. About 4-5 m with the pedestal: 4.5 m. Front (hands clasped, medallion) is -x.

models.name: Thomas Starr King, Golden Gate Park
models.description: Bronze Thomas Starr King (1892) in his frock coat holding back a cloak, on a red granite pedestal.
models.notes: Untextured: bronze. About 2.5 m figure plus a thin slab base = 2.7 m, on a red granite pedestal about 2.4 m (the model has no pedestal). Front (face and papers) is -x.

models.name: Time Signature, Foundry Square
models.description: Five stacked, curved stainless-steel vessels (2008), 48 ft tall, in front of 400 Howard Street, Foundry Square.
models.notes: Textured (grey steel). 48 ft (14.6 m) per the artist's site. An abstract stack with no real front; +z chosen. Big-monument LOD budget.

models.name: Venus, Trinity Place
models.description: 92 ft (28 m) stainless-steel Venus, a twisting modern take on the Venus de Milo, in the piazza of Trinity Place, 8th and Market (2016).
models.notes: Textured dark steel. OSM height 28 m; press says 92 ft. Front taken as the side that shows the shoulders (-x), by judgement.

models.name: Verdi Monument, Music Concourse
models.description: Gilded bronze bust of Giuseppe Verdi on a granite pylon with a bronze allegorical group, on a stepped platform (1914), Golden Gate Park.
models.notes: Textured. about.md: roughly 5 m total; the model includes its stepped granite platform, so no plinth. Front (bust and bronze group) is -x.

models.name: Volunteer Firemen Memorial, Washington Square
models.description: Bronze group of three volunteer firemen, one pointing aloft, one carrying a rescued woman (1933), on a round stone pedestal in Washington Square.
models.notes: Untextured: copperoxide (green-patinated bronze, per the Commons photo). About 3 m group on its low bronze base; the model has no stone pedestal, so a 1.5 m plinth. Front (the pointing fireman) is -x.

models.name: Wave Heart, Ocean Beach
models.description: Heart-shaped sculpture of two sweeping wave forms (2025), Ocean Beach.
models.notes: Textured (dark wood/bronze). No source for its size found: sized 1.4 m tall (about 2 m wide), like the 5 ft Hearts in SF pieces. Flat form: faces +x/-x identically; +x chosen.

models.name: Yoda Fountain, Letterman Digital Arts Center
models.description: Bronze Yoda on a faceted stone pedestal, Letterman Digital Arts Center, Presidio (2005).
models.notes: Textured. Overall 2.5 m, matching the procedural fountain (presidio.json). The model is the pedestal and Yoda; Yoda faces -x.

models.name: St Francis Hugging the Globe, St Mary's Cathedral
models.description: Bronze St Francis kneeling and embracing the world, on a relief-carved block (unveiled 2026), the plaza of St Mary's Cathedral.
models.notes: Textured bronze. About 2 m overall including its block (brief estimate). The kneeling figure faces +z toward the globe.
